svg.title: Emergency Ring architecture
svg.desc: A Shortcut sends a trigger with a secret token to a Lambda function in AWS. The Lambda keeps an incident record in DynamoDB, uses an SQS delayed message as its repeat timer, places a call through Twilio and sends a Pushover alert. Both services call back to the Lambda, which checks each callback. The call travels over the cellular voice network or Wi-Fi Calling and the push over internet data, so either path can fail without silencing the alert. By default the push fires first, the call 30 seconds later, and each repeats every 90 seconds. Acknowledging either one stops both: pressing 1 on a call retracts the push, and acknowledging the push hangs up a ringing call. A second, quieter tier called break-glass lets an assistant agent send one gentle, rate-limited alert through the same function, with its own token and never a call. A kill switch lets the owner pause everything: the active alert is stopped and new ones are refused until the pause ends, which it always does by itself. A monthly self-test, started by a timer or an agent, runs a labelled drill through the whole path, and optional alarms email when the function fails or spending passes the budget.
svg.text: A red button on the sender's phone makes the owner's ring through silent mode until acknowledged, or about 8 minutes.
Rear-ended at a red light. Nobody hurt, car disabled.

Press 1 on the call, or tap
Defaults shown. Every timing is a setting, and either arm can be switched off.
Answering without pressing 1 does not count, because voicemail can answer too.
Break-glass: a quieter tier for an agent
At most one alert per 15 minutes and 8 a day by default. Anything sooner is refused and never reaches the phone.
An agent's token cannot start an emergency.
Kill switch: if it will not stop ringing

g.text: Call hung up, push retracted, new alerts refused

svg.text: A pause lasts 60 minutes by default and a day at most. It always ends by itself, so alerting cannot be left off
by accident. A sender who triggers during a pause is told it failed, and their Shortcut sends its backup alert.

g.text: Why it is built this way
A contact set to Emergency Bypass
too, and show the text and a map.
Cell voice and internet data fail
separately, so one can get through.
Voicemail can answer a call, but
Only a sender's token can start
Nothing to patch or keep running,
and close to free at this scale.
